summary: Steel lookout in Clinton County: site given in 1954, built that winter, first used in 1955. No source found describes the site today.

events.note: Built in the winter of 1954, per the February 1970 account. The July 1954 plan was for an 80-foot steel tower.
First used in the spring of 1955; William H. Peercy was the first lookout watchman.
A June 1956 item names Earl T. Denney as the regular lookout.

evidence.supports: Bruce Sloan gave a lookout tower site to the Division of Forestry (July 1954)
evidence.quote: Bruce Sloan, President of the Sloan Coal Company, has given a lookout tower site to the Division of Forestry.

evidence.supports: Site at the heads of Duvall Valley and Gap Creek
evidence.quote: This site is at the heads of Duvall Valley and Gap Creek.

evidence.supports: Planned 80-foot steel tower on a tenth-acre site (July 1954)
evidence.quote: It is planned to build an 80 foot fire lookout steel tower on this tenth acre site.

evidence.supports: Planned to be the highest tower in the Cumberland River Fires Control Unit
evidence.quote: This will be the highest tower in the Cumberland River Fires Control Unit.
Bids have been opened to the 60-ft. fire lookout towers.

evidence.supports: September 1954 notice placed the tower at the heads of Duvall Valley and Gay Creek
evidence.quote: One will be located on the Clinton County line at the heads of Duvall Valley and Gay Creek.

evidence.supports: The towers were steel and would be erected soon
evidence.quote: These steel towers will be erected soon.

evidence.supports: Built in the winter of 1954, first used in the spring of 1955
evidence.quote: The tower was built in the winter of 1954 and first used in the spring of 1955.

evidence.supports: William H. Peercy helped build the tower and was the first lookout watchman
evidence.quote: William H. Peercy helped build the tower and was the first lookout watchman.

evidence.supports: Peercy later was dispatcher and fire crew leader
evidence.quote: Later Peercy was dispatcher and fire crewleader.

evidence.supports: Henry Foster and Bruce Sloan donated the location and road
evidence.quote: The location of Savage forest fire lookout tower and the road way to it was donated by Henry Foster and Bruce Sloan.

evidence.supports: June 1956: Earl T. Denney, regular lookout, discovered most of the fires
evidence.quote: The regular fire lookout at Savage Tower, Earl T. Denney, discovered most of the fires.

evidence.supports: Five fires reported on duty; one reported after going off duty
evidence.quote: He reported five while on duty and drove to town to report one after he had gone off duty.

evidence.supports: Savage is in Clinton County (page heading)

sources.title: Savage - FOREST LOOKOUTS, quoting Clinton County News items of 1954, 1956 and 1970

notes_for_editor: One source: a Forest Lookouts page quoting Clinton County News items (1954, 1956, 1970). Not on the NHLR Kentucky list or the FFLOS Kentucky former-site list (checked). Two searches found no current status, so the story gives no fate or access. Record height_m 24.4 m equals the July 1954 plan of 80 ft; the September 1954 notice says 60-ft towers and no source confirms the built height, so facts omit height. Creek spelled Gap Creek (July) and Gay Creek (September). facts.agency uses the Division of Forestry wording from the 1954 article; the source does not name the state agency further. Lede no longer says Kentucky: no quoted source names the state (the page shows Clinton County only), so the state was dropped from the story rather than sourced. Story now says Savage 'was' a lookout (no source confirms it stands today).
